command:
cat <<'EOF' > setup-git-web-server.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail

# Run as root, optionally setting GIT_USER to the SSH account that will push.
GIT_USER="${GIT_USER:-${SUDO_USER:-}}"
REPO="${GIT_REPO:-/git/server}"
WEB_ROOT="${WEB_ROOT:-/var/www/git-server}"
UNIT="${SYSTEMD_UNIT_FILE:-/etc/systemd/system/git-web.service}"

if [[ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo "Run as root (for example: sudo GIT_USER=deploy $0)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ -z "$GIT_USER" ]] || ! id "$GIT_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Set GIT_USER to an existing SSH account that will push." >&2
  exit 1
fi
for cmd in git python3 systemctl; do
  command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing required command: $cmd" >&2; exit 1; }
done

GIT_HOME="$(getent passwd "$GIT_USER" | cut -d: -f6)"
[[ -n "$GIT_HOME" ]] || { echo "Could not find home directory for $GIT_USER" >&2; exit 1; }
WEB_ROOT="$(realpath -m "$WEB_ROOT")"
REPO="$(realpath -m "$REPO")"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$REPO")" "$WEB_ROOT"
if [[ ! -d "$REPO" ]]; then
  git init --bare --initial-branch=master "$REPO"
fi
chown -R "$GIT_USER":"$(id -gn "$GIT_USER")" "$REPO" "$WEB_ROOT"

mkdir -p "$REPO/hooks"
cat > "$REPO/hooks/post-receive" <<HOOK
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail
while read -r oldrev newrev ref; do
  [[ "\$ref" == "refs/heads/master" ]] || continue
  if [[ "\$newrev" == "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]]; then
    echo "Refusing to deploy a deleted master branch." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  git --git-dir="$REPO" --work-tree="$WEB_ROOT" checkout -f master
  # Remove files deleted from the deployed branch, without touching server-owned extras.
  git --git-dir="$REPO" --work-tree="$WEB_ROOT" ls-files -z --deleted | xargs -0 -r rm -f --
done
HOOK
chmod 0755 "$REPO/hooks/post-receive"
chown "$GIT_USER":"$(id -gn "$GIT_USER")" "$REPO/hooks/post-receive"

cat > "$UNIT" <<UNITFILE
[Unit]
Description=Static website deployed from the Git server repository
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=$GIT_USER
Group=$(id -gn "$GIT_USER")
WorkingDirectory=$WEB_ROOT
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 0.0.0.0 --directory $WEB_ROOT
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNITFILE
chmod 0644 "$UNIT"
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now git-web.service

echo "Ready: git clone $GIT_USER@$(hostname):$REPO"
echo "Push to master; published files are served from http://$(hostname):8080/"
EOF
chmod +x setup-git-web-server.sh
cat <<'EOF' > README.md
# Git-push static web server

`setup-git-web-server.sh` configures a Linux server with systemd, Git, and Python 3. It creates a bare SSH-push repository at `/git/server`, deploys pushes to `master` into `/var/www/git-server`, and serves that directory on TCP port 8080.

On the server, run as root, setting the existing SSH account that will push:

```sh
sudo GIT_USER=your-ssh-user ./setup-git-web-server.sh
```

The account needs SSH access and permission to push to the repository. Configure its SSH login separately. Ensure firewall/network rules permit inbound TCP 8080.

From a client:

```sh
git clone your-ssh-user@server:/git/server
cd server
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
```

The web service runs as the SSH account, restarts on failure, and serves only the deployed document root. Set `GIT_REPO`, `WEB_ROOT`, or `SYSTEMD_UNIT_FILE` when installing to customize paths.
EOF
